ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, a circle $\odot O$ with diameter $AB$ exactly passes through point $C$, and $AC$ and $DO$ intersect at point $E$. It is known that $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, and $CD:BC=2:\sqrt{5}$. What is the value of $CE:AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OC\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of the circle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACB=$\angle$ADC=90$^\circ$,\\
$\because$ AC bisects $\angle$BAD,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAC=$\angle$CAB, $\angle$DAB=2$\angle$CAB,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADC\sim \triangle ACB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{AD}{AC}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-AC^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}AB$, $AD=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}AC=\frac{4}{5}AB$\\
$\therefore$ $CD=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}BC=\frac{2}{5}AB$,\\
Also $\because$ $\angle$BOC=2$\angle$CAB,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BOC=$\angle$DAB,\\
$\therefore$ AD$\parallel$OC,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle OCE\sim \triangle DAE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CE}{AE}=\frac{OC}{DA}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}AB}{\frac{4}{5}AB}=\boxed{\frac{5}{8}}$,\\

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows a circle with horizontal diameter AB and center O on AB. Point C lies on the upper-right part of the circle. Segment AC is drawn from A to C, and point D is above the circle/near the top, with segments AD and DC forming quadrilateral ABCD. A line through D and O intersects AC at E, consistent with E lying on both DO and AC. The visual also supports connecting O to C as an auxiliary radius. Reasoning following the assigned method: Connect OC. Since AB is a diameter of the circle and C lies on the circle, by Thales' theorem ∠ACB = 90°. Given ∠ADC = 90°, and AC bisects ∠BAD, we have ∠DAC = ∠CAB. Thus right triangles △ADC and △ACB are similar, with correspondences D ↔ C and C ↔ B. Therefore CD/BC = AD/AC = AC/AB. Given CD:BC = 2:√5, we get AC/AB = 2/√5, so AC = (2/√5)AB = (2√5/5)AB. Also AD/AC = 2/√5, hence AD = (2/√5)AC = (2/√5)(2√5/5)AB = (4/5)AB. Next, because ∠BOC is the central angle subtending arc BC and ∠BAC is the corresponding inscribed angle, ∠BOC = 2∠BAC. Since AC bisects ∠BAD, ∠DAB = 2∠CAB = 2∠BAC. Hence ∠BOC = ∠DAB. With OB collinear with AB, this gives AD ∥ OC. Now E lies on both AC and DO. Since AD ∥ OC, triangles △OCE and △DAE are similar. Thus CE/AE = OC/AD. Because OC is a radius and AB is a diameter, OC = AB/2. Therefore CE/AE = (AB/2)/((4/5)AB) = 5/8. So CE:AE = 5:8.
